profile.reading:
Per CyrusOne's own campus page, NYM5 sits at 6 Norden Place, Norwalk, CT 06855, publishing 168,000 sq ft and 4 MW of total IT capacity; CyrusOne's own locations page describes this as Connecticut's largest data center.

Wikipedia's CyrusOne entry states the company acquired Cervalis, a Connecticut-area data center and colocation provider, in July 2015 for approximately $400 million, the likely origin of CyrusOne's presence in this Connecticut/Hudson Valley New York cluster (which also includes a Wappingers Falls, NY facility tracked elsewhere in this registry); CyrusOne was founded in July 2000 by David Ferdman and Larry Bursten and was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and Global Infrastructure Partners (GIP) acquired the company for approximately $15 billion.

Since going private under KKR and GIP ownership in 2022, CyrusOne has continued expanding its US and international footprint; the company's own press materials cite roughly $1 billion in cumulative capital investment in its San Antonio, Texas campuses alone as of a January 2025 groundbreaking, indicating continued growth investment across its portfolio under private ownership rather than a broad slowdown following the take-private transaction.

In November 2021, KKR and GIP first announced the agreement to acquire CyrusOne in an approximately $15 billion transaction, one of the largest data center M&A deals of that period, reflecting broader private-equity and infrastructure-fund interest in colocation real estate that has also driven acquisitions of peers like QTS (by Blackstone) and CoreSite (by American Tower) around the same era; CyrusOne's current published portfolio language describes more than 50 mission-critical facilities worldwide, though the company's own site and Wikipedia give somewhat different approximate totals (over 40 versus more than 50), neither of which this registry treats as a precise, independently verified figure.

reading.body:
CyrusOne Norwalk (NYM5) holds 4 MW of published IT capacity across 168,000 square feet in Norwalk, Connecticut. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this is roughly 100 racks. The facility's total MW is not published, so the IT load represents only a disclosed portion of the campus.

Norwalk ranks first among Connecticut's five mapped data center facilities by published capacity and accounts for half of the state's 8 MW of published IT load. Connecticut's two facilities with published specifications suggest limited transparency across the state's data center footprint. The campus carries SSAE 16 Type II certification, which qualifies it to host systems requiring audited security and availability controls.

The CyrusOne Norwalk campus is part of a tri-state cluster spanning Connecticut and the Hudson Valley. CyrusOne was taken private in 2022 when Kohlberg Kravis Roberts and Global Infrastructure Partners acquired it for 15 billion dollars. Without published total capacity, the campus's relevance to AI scaling depends on how much undisclosed capacity lies behind the 4 MW figure and whether this private acquisition signals deployment plans in the region.
